question: How many planets are terrestrial planets?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The solar system **comprises **four terrestrial planets**:** Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars**, which also happen to be the four nearest to the sun.
 
• **Terrestrial planets**, also referred to as** "telluric planets"** or "rocky planets," feature a solid, rocky surface akin to Earth's terra firma.
 
• These planets typically possess a dense, metallic core primarily composed of iron, along with a silicate mantle layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Within the Solar System, the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)** recognizes the terrestrial planets as the inner planets closest to the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
 
• **Mercury, **the smallest planet in the Solar System, holds the position of the closest planet to the Sun.
 
• **Venus,** the second planet from the Sun, shares many similarities with Earth, being a terrestrial planet and comparable in mass and size to its neighboring planet.
 
• **Earth,** positioned as the third planet from the Sun, stands as a unique celestial body known for its capacity to support life. Its abundance of liquid surface water distinguishes it as a water world, a feature absent in other planets within the Solar System.
 
• **Mars**, known as the fourth planet from the Sun, earned the moniker "the Red Planet" due to the iron(III) oxide dust covering its surface, resulting in its distinctive orange-red appearance.
